headline: United States Loses Measles Elimination Status Amid Record Outbreak
metaDescription: The Pan American Health Organization revoked the measles-elimination status of the United States following a record-breaking surge in reported cases.
aiSummaryBullets: The Pan American Health Organization revoked the United States' measles-elimination status after over 5,400 cases were recorded in 2026.
Current infection numbers represent the highest rate of viral spread in the country since 1991, according to international health officials.
Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles-free designations as vaccination rates decline across the Americas.
aiContextParagraph: The United States has officially lost its measles-elimination status after 26 years, a designation awarded to countries that have interrupted the continuous transmission of the virus for more than 12 months. This development follows a significant rise in infections, with 2026 case numbers more than doubling the totals reported in the previous year. Global health authorities attribute this trend to declining vaccination coverage both within the United States and across the Americas, where measles has been circulating since 2024. The loss of status is marked by the worst outbreak in the country since 1991. The Pan American Health Organization confirmed that other nations, specifically Mexico and Bolivia, have also lost their measles-free status during this period of rising contagion and increasing deaths. Public health experts describe this backslide as a notable challenge for national and regional disease control efforts.
whyItIsViral: This story is trending due to extensive coverage from ten independent news outlets and high viral activity across global media.
